title: Divide and Conquer Recursion Tree
description: A four-level decimation-in-time tree splitting eight samples by index parity down to single samples, with click-to-highlight paths and a staged reveal animation.
creator: Real-Time DSP on a $5 Microcontroller
author: Dan McCreary
subject: Digital Signal Processing
FFT
Algorithms

learningObjectives: Interpret the recursive even/odd split of a DFT problem
Explain what happens at each level and why recursion stops at size 1
prerequisites: A DFT maps N inputs to N outputs

controls.label: Play split animation
controls.purpose: Reveal the tree one level at a time

controls.label: Any node
controls.purpose: Highlight the path back to the root and describe the subsequence

equations: even/odd split by position within the subsequence
assumptions: Decimation in time rather than in frequency
limitations: Shows the split only; the recombination butterflies that follow appear in the FFT stage sims

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Whole-structure diagram with click-triggered path highlighting
keyQuestions: Why does the recursion stop at a single sample?
Why is the bottom row not in sorted order?
commonMisconceptions: That the splitting itself is where the computational saving comes from
That FFT output arrives in natural index order
assessmentOpportunities: Predict tree depth and leaf position for a 16-point FFT
